author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN002475783 (PTHR11022)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel CG9380 (FBgn0035094) Q0E8V8

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation, or other issue**

PTHR11022 includes 14 Dmel proteins - 13 are known PGRP (PEPTIDOGLYCAN-RECOGNITION PROTEIN) proteins with known roles in immunity etc.
The extra gene/protein is CG9380 (FBgn0035094) Q0E8V8.
Unlike the other genes, this one has no computed orthologs, paralogs or InterPro domains.
And BLASTing the CG9380 protein sequence against all Dmel proteins only gives itself as a significant hit.

So, could you look into why CG9380 is in PTHR11022 and getting annotated with the 5 GO terms annotated to PTN002475783.

Thanks!
title: PAINT issue: PTN002475783 (PTHR11022)

author: marcfeuermann
body: This is how the tree looks like for the Drosophila sequences (after reviewing). I think the best would be not to PAINT such regions.

author: sjm41
body:
Thanks Marc!
That's a tricky looking tree....but reassuring to see that CG9380 is clearly distinct from the other Dmel genes.

author: sjm41
body:
Hi @marcfeuermann 

Just checking on this - I still see the original problem, that CG9380 (FBgn0035094/Q0E8V8) gets N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine amidase activity via PTN002475783.

And it looks like the paint node still has that MF here:
https://pantree.org/node/annotationNode.jsp?id=PTN002475783

Is that expected, or should the "N-acetylmuramoyl-L-alanine amidase activity" annotation to CG9380 have disappeared by now?

author: marcfeuermann
body: Hello Steven, I checked the annotation, and it hasn't changed since it was corrected (see the figure). So from my end, it looks fine. It's probably just a delay issue. I’ve sometimes had to wait between 6 and 9 months for primary annotations to appear so I can use them with PAINT. That’s why I asked to be able to create them directly with PAINT. But I have no control over the reverse process ;-) I’ll leave the ticket open, and we’ll close it when my corrections finally appear. Best regards, Marc

author: sjm41
body:
OK, thanks for checking. I normally see your corrections within a couple of months within FlyBase, but this one was 6 months ago.
Actually, checking in Protein2GO (which I should have done before!) does show that the previous IBA annotations have gone, so this must just be a downstream updating issue.
I'll re-close this ticket after all.
Sorry to bother you!

author: marcfeuermann
body: No worries Steven. you did not bother me. It's my job and I enjoy exchanging with my collaborators... especially when it's about an easy task for me ;-)
